newsitem.title: IRAQ: UNICEF says many Iraqis suffer malnutrition.
newsitem.headline: UNICEF says many Iraqis suffer malnutrition.

text.p: The United Nations Children's fund UNICEF said on Thursday one out of every four Iraqi children is suffering from severe chronic malnutrition.

UNCIEF, quoting a survey it conducted recently with the World Health Organisation and the Iraqi Health Ministry, said the most vulnerable group was children under five years; 27.5 per cent of those surveyed were malnourished.
"One out of every four young Iraqi children is malnourished," UNICEF said in a news release distributed to foreign reporters.
"The survey was conducted in 87 primary health care centres in 15 (Iraqi) governorates in the centre and south of Iraq," it added.

Crippling United Nations sanctions imposed on Iraq after its 1990 invasion of Kuwait have left many Iraqis desperate for food and medical supplies. Food and medical imports are exempt from the sanctions but their arrival has lagged.
"In 1991, one year after the sanctions began, only 9.2 per cent of children were found to be malnourished," the survey noted.
Under an oil-for-food deal with the U.N., Iraq has been allowed since December to sell $2 billion worth of oil to satisfy the urgent needs of Iraqis. The deal is due for review in June.
Iraq announced on Thursday a cut on the monthly food rations distributed to its citizens at subsidised prices because of delays in the arrival of foodstuffs.
